result.title: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models
result.summary: Comparative feedback, in which a judge says which of two candidate outcomes is closer to what happened, is a practical way to train language world models that assign probabilities to an action's outcomes. We show that, fitted with a Bradley-Terry objective, it need not teach the true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones. On a simulated robot push with enumerated outcome distributions, this objective takes a model that is accurate on unseen layouts (hazard error 2.4 percentage points, pp) and moves 33 to 43 pp of its probability onto outcomes that none of a condition's enumerated branches produces. The cause is the objective, not the comparisons: its optimum, computed before training, predicts where the model ends up, and a likelihood that knows the judge's rule learns from the same comparisons without the shift. The shift is robust: it recurs on unseen conditions, under five candidate laws and a three-fold denser enumeration, and about 29 pp remain without the physically impossible events. Its cost is conditional: with those events it inflates hazard probabilities, and a threshold inherited from the pre-feedback model costs about 3 pp of utility per decision on trained and 1 to 2 pp on unseen conditions, through false rejects; without them the utility loss averages below 1 pp over six seeds, though a small regret in action choice remains. Audits of readout, response and decision trace the effect from probabilities to actions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验用 Bradley-Terry 目标从比较反馈训练语言世界模型是否会歪曲本已准确的结果概率：在模拟机器人推动任务中，该目标把 33–43 个百分点的概率质量转到枚举分支都产生不了的结果上，并定位为目标函数最优点所致而非比较数据本身。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「比较式偏好监督的最优解可能系统性偏离真实结果分布，而知晓评判规则的似然训练不会」的结论，可供核查 LVR 中以比较反馈或偏好目标监督 latent 状态与推理轨迹时的概率校准和贡献分配风险。
